description: Companion script that normalizes folder timestamps so each repo directory's mtime matches its latest git commit date. Scans all subdirectories of the target path, reads the latest commit timestamp via git log, and applies it via fs.utimesSync. Supports --dry-run to preview changes without modifying timestamps. Reports oldest/newest folders and skipped (non-git, no-commit) entries in formatted tables.
notes: Backfilled by feature-coverage-audit from current implementation evidence on 2026-06-10.
Bare catch fixed via folded code-quality audit finding (consolidated 2026-06-11).
spec:
1. Verify running set-folder-dates updates each repo folder's mtime to its latest git commit date.
2. Verify --dry-run prints the would-be changes without modifying timestamps.
3. Verify non-git directories are skipped with status 'skipped:not-git'.
4. Verify git directories with no commits are skipped with status 'skipped:no-commit'.
5. Verify the output includes a count of updated/would-update and skipped folders.
6. Verify oldest and newest timestamp tables are displayed when changes are made.
7. Verify the catch block handling git log / fs.utimesSync failures uses `catch (err)` (never a bare `catch {}`) and logs a console.warn with the folder name and error message (`Cannot process ${entry.name}: ${(err as Error).message}`) before recording the skipped result — errors must not be silently swallowed.
title: Folder Date Normalization
